name: Glider flight (lift, stall, thermals)
what: A hang glider's flight model: the pilot sets angle of attack and bank, lift grows with airspeed squared, drag has parasitic and induced parts, the wing stalls when slow and nose-high, a g limit caps pull-ups. The air moves: a gusty breeze, thermals that lean and breathe, ridge lift on windward slopes, sink over water. Skimming low is efficient (ground effect and a skim cushion); a flare past the stall is the landing. An autopilot flies scripted routes with the player's inputs and runs in Node to prove a level is flyable. Also a lighter arcade kite mode that never stalls.
use_when: the player flies, glides or soars without an engine (hang glider, paraglider, bird, wingsuit, paper plane, kite) and height for speed, lift, stall, finding rising air and landing should matter
good_for: Hang gliding, paragliding and soaring games; birds that ride thermals; wingsuit and paper-plane games that want real energy and stall; any game where the fun is reading the air and landing well. The autopilot and the Node simulator let an agent tune and prove a route without a browser. Kite mode covers fast, forgiving racing flight through lanes, with boosts, slipstreams and wall scrapes that cost speed instead of ending the run.
not_for: Powered aircraft and dogfights steered by pointing the mouse (use meticulai-arcade-flight), helicopters or hovering, full rigid-body flight sims with control surfaces, space flight.
how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs meticulai-glider-flight, then build a world object (heightAt, wind, thermals), createGlider(world) from vendor/meticulai-glider-flight/src/glider.js and step it at 120 Hz with createInput(canvas).update(dt); see HOW-TO-USE.md
